title: Reasons by size
description: Subset-minimal sufficient reasons, smallest first. The abstraction is asked for a smallest candidate; when the check finds no counterexample the candidate is a solution, and a helper solver writes the clause that removes all its supersets, since a failed check leaves no model to read a refinement from. Because candidates come in order of size, each of the 4 accepted sets is minimal.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The network's answer on the input. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
% feature(F), unit(U), weight(U,F,W), threshold(U,T), vote(U,V), and the input is(F,B).
% The network's answer on this input.
fires0(U) :- threshold(U,T), #sum { W,F : weight(U,F,W), is(F,1) } >= T.
yes0 :- #sum { V,U : vote(U,V), fires0(U) } >= 3.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): sets of features, smallest first.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a set of features whose values are kept, as small as possible
% (the loop asks solver A for an optimal model).
{ keep(F) : feature(F) }.
#minimize { 1,F : keep(F) }.
#show keep/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the kept features.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for an input that agrees on the kept features and gets the other answer (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: another input x/1 that agrees with the given one on the kept
% features ...
{ x(F) } :- feature(F).
:- keep(F), is(F,1), not x(F).
:- keep(F), is(F,0), x(F).
% ... but gets the other answer from the network.
fires(U) :- threshold(U,T), #sum { W,F : weight(U,F,W), x(F) } >= T.
yes :- #sum { V,U : vote(U,V), fires(U) } >= 3.
:- yes, yes0.
:- not yes, not yes0.
differs(F) :- is(F,1), not x(F).
differs(F) :- is(F,0), x(F).
#show x/1.
#show differs/1.

% The input refutes every set of kept features on which it agrees with the given
% input. So one of the features on which it differs has to be kept.
relevant(keep(F)) :- differs(F).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G  = A -> C via shared + glue

# Smallest candidates first: A.solve(optimal) returns a smallest set that is still
# possible. If the check finds no counterexample, the set is a sufficient reason, and
# all its supersets are sufficient too: G.above(M) removes M and its supersets. Because
# candidates come smallest first, each accepted set is minimal.
loop:
    M = A.solve(optimal)
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.above(M))

% A small network over 8 binary features. A hidden unit fires when the weighted sum of
% its inputs reaches its threshold; the answer is "yes" when the weighted sum of the
% firing units reaches 3.
feature(1..8).
unit(1..3).
% weight(U,F,W): unit U sees feature F with weight W.
weight(1,1,-2). weight(1,3,1). weight(1,4,-1). weight(1,6,-3). weight(1,7,-3). weight(1,8,-1).
weight(2,1,-3). weight(2,3,2). weight(2,4,-2). weight(2,5,-3). weight(2,6,-2). weight(2,7,-1).
weight(2,8,3).
weight(3,1,-2). weight(3,2,3). weight(3,3,2).  weight(3,5,-3). weight(3,7,-1). weight(3,8,3).
threshold(1,2). threshold(2,1). threshold(3,2).
vote(1,1). vote(2,1). vote(3,3).
% The input to be explained: is(F,B) says that feature F has the value B.
is(1,0). is(2,1). is(3,1). is(4,0). is(5,1). is(6,0). is(7,0). is(8,1).

% Majority of three: one unit fires when at least two features are 1, and its vote
% of 3 decides. On the input 1 1 1 any two features force the answer "yes".
feature(1..3).
unit(1).
weight(1,F,1) :- feature(F).
threshold(1,2).
vote(1,3).
